daily.summary: Equinor is still restoring IT systems after a cyberattack that left oil and gas production untouched; the company says no virus was involved and has not named an attacker. The FBI warned about an AI framework used to automate intrusions and detailed a large North Korean crypto-theft scheme, and Google described a Russian FSB-linked group impersonating one US victim's staff to breach another. Patching pressure is high: CISA flagged active exploitation of a Perforce Puppet flaw and urged fixes for Java4Shell, and F5 released fixes for five NGINX flaws allowing remote code execution, with no in-the-wild exploitation reported so far.

weekly.summary: The week's reporting centres on attackers using AI to speed up intrusions: the FBI, Google and Unit 42 all describe autonomous attack frameworks in real operations. State-linked activity includes North Korean financial theft, Russian espionage against Romanian government email and against two US organizations, and a reported China-linked intrusion at a European telecom provider. Equinor's IT outage is the week's most notable incident at an allied energy operator, with production reported unaffected, and critical flaws in Java, NGINX, Puppet, Cisco BroadWorks and refrigeration controllers keep patching pressure high.
